title: The T-shirt I Nearly Didn’t Buy
scene: You go into a clothing shop for one plain T-shirt, overthink the colour, get pulled into a two-for-one-style discount decision, and then discover at home that you already own two very similar shirts.
sceneJa: 無地のTシャツを1枚だけ買うつもりで服屋に入る。色を考えすぎたうえ、2枚買うと安くなると言われてさらに悩み、帰宅すると似たTシャツをすでに2枚持っていたことに気づく。

chunks.en: I went into a clothing shop
chunks.ja: 服屋に入りました

chunks.en: because I needed a plain T-shirt,
chunks.ja: 無地のTシャツが必要だったので
それは〜のように思えました
かなり簡単なミッション
ほぼすぐに1枚見つけました
ただ3色あり
どれも同じくらい無難に見えました
店の照明の下では

chunks.en: I picked up the navy one,
chunks.ja: ネイビーを手に取り
いったん戻し

chunks.en: compared it with the grey one,
chunks.ja: グレーと比べ

chunks.en: and then picked up the navy one again.
chunks.ja: そしてまたネイビーを手に取りました
数分すると
想像し始めました
どちらの色の方が合うか
ほとんど着ない服に
それはさすがに考えすぎに思えたので

chunks.en: so I decided to keep things simple
chunks.ja: シンプルに考えることにして
ネイビーを買うことにしました

chunks.en: I had chosen at the beginning.
chunks.ja: 最初に選んでいた
レジで
店員が何気なく言いました

chunks.en: that the same T-shirt was on sale
chunks.ja: 同じTシャツがセールになると
2枚買えば

chunks.en: I went back to the shelf
chunks.ja: 棚へ戻り
さらに5分使いました
何色にするかを決めるのに

chunks.en: the second unnecessary T-shirt should be.
chunks.ja: 必要のなかった2枚目のTシャツを
結局

chunks.en: I bought the navy one and the grey one,
chunks.ja: ネイビーとグレーを買い
妙に満足しながら
自分の慎重な意思決定に
家に帰ると
クローゼットを開け

chunks.en: and found two very similar T-shirts
chunks.ja: よく似たTシャツを2枚見つけました
すでにそこにあるのを

chunks.en: By the end of the day,
chunks.ja: その日が終わるころには
Tシャツが4枚になり
そして、それほど役には立ちませんが
自分の好みの一貫性には完全な自信が持てました

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: so I decided to keep things simple / and buy the navy one / I had chosen at the beginning
so I decided / to keep things / simple and buy / the navy one I had chosen at the beginning
so I / decided to keep / things simple and / buy the navy one
questions.explanation: The first version keeps the decision phrase, the action, and the description of the original choice in natural meaning groups.

questions.question: What does ‘keep things simple’ mean here?
options: Avoid making the decision more complicated than necessary
questions.explanation: ‘Keep things simple’ means avoiding unnecessary complexity. The irony is that the speaker soon makes the shopping trip complicated again.

questions.question: Why is the final sentence funny?
options: The speaker treats owning four similar shirts as proof of consistent taste rather than poor planning
The speaker is unhappy with all four shirts
The shop gave the speaker four shirts by mistake
questions.explanation: The dry humour reframes a mildly pointless purchase as reassuring evidence that the speaker’s preferences are at least consistent.

speak: Start matter-of-factly, as if buying a plain T-shirt should be easy. Let the indecision build gently rather than dramatically. Give ‘the second unnecessary T-shirt’ a small pause before ‘should be’. Read the final sentence calmly, with slight emphasis on ‘rather less usefully’ and ‘complete confidence in my consistency’.
review: Flow: simple shopping goal → unnecessary colour analysis → return to the first choice → discount creates a second decision → confident purchase → wardrobe reveals repetition → dry reframing as consistency. Useful chunks: ‘keep things simple’, ‘at the beginning’, and ‘by the end of the day’. The ending avoids a dramatic failure and instead turns repetition into a strangely positive personal finding.
